== Biography ==
'''Ann Glasgow''' married '''Andrew McClelland''', a carpenter, and the family lived at Killyless, Craigs parish, County Antrim. No record of Ann's own birth, marriage or death has been found; her children's records establish her name and identity.

Their son '''Andrew McClelland''', a weaver of Killyless, married '''Jane McCracken''' of Ballyconnelly (daughter of William McCracken, labourer) at the parish church of Craigs on 24 December 1860; the marriage names Andrew's father as '''Andrew McClelland, carpenter'''.<ref name="Andrew1860">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Craigs parish church, 24 December 1860, entry 70: Andrew McClelland, of Killyless, son of Andrew McClelland, carpenter; Jane McCracken, of Ballyconnelly, daughter of William McCracken, labourer; witnesses Samuel Thompson and John Bacchus. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1860/09582/5474474.pdf register image], group registration ID 3299926.</ref>

The same son died at Bridgeton, Lanarkshire, Scotland, on 17 January 1870, aged 35, an engine keeper; his death record names his parents as '''Andrew McClelland and Ann Glasgow'''.<ref name="AndrewDeath1870">Scotland civil registration, death, 17 January 1870, Bridgeton, Lanarkshire: Andrew McClelland, 35, engine keeper, parents Andrew McClelland and Ann Glasgow, widow Jane McCracken. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XSSG-M9CW FamilySearch XSSG-M9CW].</ref>

A second son '''Robert McLelland''', a carter aged 32, married '''Martha McLean''' (daughter of John McLean and Catherine McIlroy) on 18 July 1873; his record names his parents as '''Andrew McLelland and Ann Glasgow'''.<ref name="Robert1873">Scotland civil registration, marriage, 18 July 1873: Robert McLelland, 32, carter, parents Andrew McLelland and Ann Glasgow; bride Martha McLean. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X95J-MXQP FamilySearch X95J-MXQP].</ref>

Ann was almost certainly a sister of [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]] of Plattsburgh, New York. The 14 January 1892 probate citation in Nancy's estate lists "the children of Ann McClelland, whose names and places of residence are unknown" among Nancy's heirs and next of kin.<ref>''The Plattsburgh Sentinel'', 26 February 1892, p. 6. [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6 newspaper page]; also printed in ''The Plattsburgh Republican'', 23 January–13 February 1892.</ref>

The family's move to Glasgow, Scotland, between 1860 and 1863 — the same Bridgeton district where Ann's probable nephew [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]] settled — explains why Nancy's executors had no addresses for Ann's children.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-4090]] is assessed at 88% (probable). Ann McClelland’s children are named in Nancy’s 1892 citation, and sons’ Scottish records establish Ann Glasgow’s identity. John of Lisnagaver’s 16 November 1846 marriage names father John Glasgow farmer; the maintained 6 October identity definition represents this father, extending the supported family hypothesis without requiring the 1796 flaxgrower match.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.

Next useful test: Compare full probate kinship wording with the Irish siblings’ own parent statements.

Source basis already held: [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6 The Plattsburgh Sentinel, 26 February 1892, p. 6. newspaper page (https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6); also printed in The Plattsburgh Republican, 23 January–13 February 1892.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



Ann is reconstructed from her children's records and the probate citation. Her LNAB Glasgow rests on her sons' records naming her "Ann Glasgow" and on the placement of "Ann McClelland" among Nancy Glasgow's siblings in the citation. No own-event record (birth, marriage, death) has been located; her marriage pre-dates civil registration. Her parents are reassessed as [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow, farmer]] (uncertain) and an unknown mother.
